Q552.L1t: Pew Research Center runs cross-national surveys that ask people how they view diversity and immigration in their countries.
Q552.L2t: Pew's 2018 survey asked people in 27 countries whether growing racial, ethnic and national diversity makes their country a better place to live, a worse place, or makes no difference.
Q552.L3t: In that 2018 survey, India had one of the most positive responses of any country, with a clear majority well above half saying diversity makes it better, far higher than in most advanced economies.
Q552.L4t: About two-thirds of Indians, roughly 68%, said increasing diversity makes their country a better place to live.
Q552.L2f: The 2018 Pew survey on diversity was conducted only in Europe and North America, and the question offered just two response choices.
Q552.L3f: Pew's 2018 result for India was only slightly above half, a bare majority that is close to the global median.
Q552.L4f: Roughly 53% of Indians, a bit over half, said increasing diversity makes their country a better place to live.

Q661.L1t: Exponent rules let you simplify algebraic expressions before substituting a value for the variable.
Q661.L2t: The expression has two parts: a product of a reciprocal's fourth power with a constant and a fourth power, and a term whose exponent is a sum of integers.
Q661.L3t: The fourth power of the reciprocal times the fourth power of a cancels to 1, leaving the constant factor 2, and the exponent 2+1-3 equals zero, so the second term is a nonzero number to the zero power.
Q661.L4t: The expression equals 3, whatever nonzero value a takes, including 42.
Q661.L2f: The value a=42 matters because exponent rules only apply to such a variable when it is an even number.
Q661.L3f: The product (1/a)^4 · 2 · a^4 cancels completely to zero, and any nonzero base raised to the zero power also equals zero.
Q661.L4f: The whole expression evaluates to zero.

Q703.L1t: Rationalizing a denominator means rewriting a fraction so that no square roots remain in its denominator.
Q703.L2t: Radicals with the same radicand, such as multiples of the square root of 3, can be added together like like terms.
Q703.L3t: Each radical in the denominator simplifies to a multiple of the square root of 3, namely 6√3, 4√3 and 6√3, so the denominator is a single term, 16√3.
Q703.L4t: The fraction simplifies to the square root of 3 divided by 12.
Q703.L2f: A denominator with several radical terms can only be rationalized by multiplying by its conjugate three separate times.
Q703.L3f: Rationalizing multiplies 4 by the last radical term in the denominator, which gives the answer directly with no further division.
Q703.L4f: The simplified fraction is twice the square root of 27.
